agent.problem: The opening card has four sentences: the boat setup, “A boat trip with Jesus?”, the junk-drawer joke, and “Jesus tells them exactly where they're headed.” The opening card is limited to three sentences.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences.

agent.problem: The wrong answer “chained” is true of this same man earlier in the passage: Luke 8:29 says he had been bound with chains and shackles. It is false at the moment when he sits at Jesus' feet, but not false anywhere in the passage.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

human.problem: The two blanks in "The disciples are ___ and ___" can be filled in either order. "amazed and frightened" means exactly the same thing, but it would be marked wrong because "frightened" is set as blank 1 and "amazed" as blank 2.
human.question: When the two right words in a two-blank card can be swapped without changing the meaning, should the app accept either order, or should the card be rewritten so each blank has only one possible right word?
